idea: Week two, from the story bank: written from the tables, then corrected by two independent editors before voicing.
description: In 2023-24 income per person is level (Meghalaya ₹1,41,195, Madhya Pradesh ₹1,39,713), yet 80.6% of Meghalaya's women aged 15 to 49 have a mobile phone they use themselves against 48.5% in Madhya Pradesh (1.66 times; India 63.6%; NFHS-5 67.5% against 38.5%).
Survey estimate. Blank: Lakshadweep (small sample, not ranked) and Manipur (no NFHS-6 fact sheet yet). The table shows how much, not why.
source: Phones: share of women aged 15 to 49 who have a mobile phone that they themselves use, NFHS-6 (2023-24) state and India fact sheets, International Institute for Population Sciences (total, urban and rural columns; the NFHS-5 (2019-21) figure is printed beside it). 34 states and UTs ranked; Lakshadweep (small sample) is not ranked and Manipur has no NFHS-6 fact sheet yet. Income: per-capita net state domestic product, current prices, 2023-24, Reserve Bank of India, Handbook of Statistics on Indian States, Table 19 (33 states and UTs with data; National Statistical Office series).

done: Every figure recomputed from the tables by the writer and again by a numbers-and-rules editor; a viewer editor then reworked the hook, the closing question and any repeated line. Fixes applied before voicing: Hook carries 2023-24; the voice no longer reads as a comparison of counts of women (now 'women's phone share'); Past tense on cards 2 and 3 and on the say card; year added to the say card; Card 3 sub: earlier-survey 1.8 times now says Meghalaya's income was lower then; two new income tests carry it; Four-line hook that opened like px02 is now three lines, measure first: 'Women's own phones, 2023-24: Meghalaya 81%; Madhya Pradesh, same income: 48.5%'; Closing question 'Where does your state stand on phones?' (px01 plus two words) now 'Does your mother have her own phone?'
open: Re-read the phone row and label in the NFHS-6 state and India fact-sheet PDFs for Meghalaya, Madhya Pradesh and India (all four columns); the Madhya Pradesh NFHS-6 cell 48.5 could not be confirmed outside our file.
Hook voice has only 0.45 s spare in its 5.81 s beat; if the real voice overruns, the hook grows by one bar (Short about 41 s).
Not builder tests: 'tended to rise together' (rho 0.53) and 'sat above the trend'.
